basics.name: Ted Hyounggun Ahn
basics.label: Senior Software Engineer · Backend & AI Infrastructure
basics.summary: I build event-driven backends and reliable cloud platforms. I’m also exploring how AI agents fit into real engineering workflows.

work.name: US LINE WEBTOON
highlights: Recommendation Concept: Built a Spring MVC and Apache Spark batch job using precomputed title behavior and traffic data to test a recommendation concept.

work.name: USAA
highlights: Life-Safety Messaging at Scale: Built USAA's first reactive, event-driven communications platform. It processed 1M SMS messages per hour for urgent customer notifications during severe weather and life-threatening events.

Greenfield Modernization: Maintained a critical 35-year-old on-premises platform while helping build its distributed replacement with OpenShift and GitLab CI. Also worked on proofs of concept, shared libraries, and security patches.

work.name: Capital One
highlights: Patented Vehicle Data Pipeline: Designed and patented an event-driven pipeline that consolidated 3M+ vehicle records each day. It replaced a 15-year-old system and supplied data for analytics and ML features.

Reliability Under Pressure: Automated a patch and traced memory and thread leaks that threatened a high-visibility launch. The work helped prevent an outage and received the organization's inaugural award.

work.name: Capital One
highlights: High-Priority Product Delivery: Independently delivered a high-priority digital marketing pilot using spec-driven development. Its success helped establish a dedicated cross-functional team while parallel work stayed on track.
AI-Assisted Engineering: Co-developed knowledge systems and reusable context workflows for teams adopting AI-assisted development under enterprise governance.
Architecture and SRE Leadership: Automated failover and regional-isolation tests for cloud services to strengthen reliability standards.

education.summary: Built the computer science foundation that continues to guide my work in distributed systems and software architecture.

education.studyType: Postgraduate Certificate, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
education.summary: Formalized my applied ML foundation while expanding from large-scale backend engineering into model training and ML infrastructure.

skills.name: GitLab CI, GitHub Actions & developer enablement

projects.name: Ditto Factory
projects.description: An agent workflow platform that separates deterministic orchestration from model reasoning.
highlights: The repository includes workflow code and test instructions. This is a personal platform experiment; production adoption and organizational-scale reliability are not established.

projects.name: Marketplace Matching Engine
projects.description: An AI-assisted reconstruction exploring order matching, deterministic replay, and recovery under failure.
highlights: The repository documents conservation, determinism, idempotency, and failover checks. This is a plausible reconstruction from public material, not Valve’s implementation or a claim of production-scale operation.

fieldNotes.name: Testing architectural understanding through implementation
fieldNotes.summary: Using AI-assisted reconstructions to test architectural understanding: how a model finds context, handles constraints, and exposes the limits of its implementation. These are bounded learning experiments.
fieldNotes.question: Can a model demonstrate that it understands a real architecture by reconstructing its critical path?

fieldNotes.name: From agent architecture to enterprise workflows
fieldNotes.summary: The thinking behind OpenHarness and Ditto Factory: deterministic workflow control, scoped agent execution, and the gap between a proposal and a working platform.
fieldNotes.question: What survives when an agent workflow moves from architecture notes into a working platform?

fieldNotes.name: When does a dynamic agent team help?
fieldNotes.summary: An experiment comparing single-agent, static-team, and dynamic-team approaches. Runtime composition proved feasible in observed probes, but instrumentation limits prevented a defensible claim of dynamic superiority.
fieldNotes.question: Can we measure the benefit of delegation separately from failures in the measurement system?
